decouverte.titre: The bike and the game account
paragraphes: Your bike is stolen outside school. The police call it a crime. A crime is an act that the law forbids and punishes.
A few days later, someone enters your game account and takes your items. There is no thief in the street. There is only a computer and the internet.
This is also a crime. When a crime uses computers or the internet, we call it cybercrime.

decouverte.comme: A thief can use a crowbar to open a door. The thief can also steal the crowbar. In the first case, the crowbar is the tool. In the second case, it is the target.
decouverte.enVrai: In cybercrime, the computer can be the tool, for example to send a scam. It can also be the target, for example when someone steals its data. One computer can be both at the same time.

decouverte.question: Someone attacks a shop's website to put it offline. What is the website in this crime?
options: It is the tool of the crime
It is the target of the crime
It is not part of the crime
decouverte.answer: It is the target of the crime
decouverte.explanation: The attack aims at the website, so it is the target. The tool is the attacker's computer. The first answer is tempting, because a computer is always present in a cybercrime.

decouverte.comme: In a city, a thief can go after a person, a house, or the town hall. These are three different victims.
decouverte.enVrai: The manual puts cybercrimes in three groups, based on the victim: people, property, and government. One act, like hacking, can fit in more than one group. Hacking means breaking into a computer without permission. An attack on a government is an attack on the right of a whole country to rule itself.

decouverte.texte: Cyberstalking means following and watching a person online, again and again. Online harassment means insulting or threatening them. Identity theft means pretending to be them. Credit card fraud means paying with their card.
A chain of shops is hacked. Strangers copy the names and card numbers of its customers. Nobody broke a window, but data was taken without permission. This is a data breach.
Some hackers attack to share a political message. For example, they block a ministry's website to protest. This is called hacktivism. Their goal is not money. Their goal is to make a point.

cards.question: Official definition: “cybercrime”
cards.answer: A cybercrime is any criminal activity that directly involves computers or the internet.
cards.explanation: If a computer or the internet is at the heart of a crime, it is a cybercrime.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Cybercrimes and Data Breaches”. You will need to know this sentence word for word.

cards.question: Which sentence is the official definition of “cybercrime”?
options: A cybercrime is any criminal activity that only involves computers owned by companies.
A cybercrime is any criminal activity that directly involves computers or the internet.
A cybercrime is any criminal activity that indirectly involves computers or the internet.
A cybercrime is any activity, legal or not, that directly involves computers or the internet.
options_why: It adds a limit. The real sentence says computers or the internet, with no limit on who owns them.
One word is changed. The real sentence says directly: the computer is at the heart of the crime.
A legal activity is not a crime. The real sentence talks about criminal activity.
cards.answer: A cybercrime is any criminal activity that directly involves computers or the internet.
cards.explanation: Three ideas: any criminal activity, directly, computers or the internet.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “cybercrime” from memory.
cards.answer: A cybercrime is any criminal activity that directly involves computers or the internet.
cards.explanation: Three ideas: any criminal activity, directly, computers or the internet.

cards.question: Official definition: “data breach”
cards.answer: A data breach is a specific cybercrime where information is accessed or stolen by a cybercriminal without authorization.
cards.explanation: It is a special kind of cybercrime. Someone takes or looks at information without the right to do it.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Cybercrimes and Data Breaches”. The manual says the target is the information system and the data inside it.

cards.question: Which sentence is the official definition of “data breach”?
options: A data breach is a specific cybercrime where information is accessed or stolen by a cybercriminal without authorization.
A data breach is a specific cybercrime where information is accessed or stolen by an employee with authorization.
A data breach is a general cybercrime where information is deleted or changed by a cybercriminal without authorization.
A data breach is a specific cybercrime where a computer is damaged by a cybercriminal without authorization.
options_why: A cybercriminal who has no permission is the key idea. With permission, it is not a breach.
Two words are changed. A breach is about information that is accessed or stolen, not deleted or changed.
A breach targets the information in the system. Damage to the computer is a different idea.
cards.answer: A data breach is a specific cybercrime where information is accessed or stolen by a cybercriminal without authorization.
cards.explanation: Three ideas: a specific cybercrime, information accessed or stolen, without authorization.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “data breach” from memory.
cards.answer: A data breach is a specific cybercrime where information is accessed or stolen by a cybercriminal without authorization.
cards.explanation: Three ideas: a specific cybercrime, information accessed or stolen, without authorization.

cards.question: Official definition: “crimes against people”
cards.answer: Crimes against people: These crimes include cyberstalking, online harassment, identity theft, and credit card fraud.
cards.explanation: The victim is a person. Someone follows them, insults them, takes their identity, or uses their card.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Cybercrimes and Data Breaches”. This is the first of the three groups of cybercrimes.

cards.question: Say the official sentence about “crimes against people” from memory.
cards.answer: Crimes against people: These crimes include cyberstalking, online harassment, identity theft, and credit card fraud.
cards.explanation: Four examples: cyberstalking, online harassment, identity theft, credit card fraud.

cards.question: Official definition: “crimes against property”
cards.answer: Crimes against property: Property in this case may include information stored within a computer, or the computer itself.
cards.explanation: Property is what belongs to you. It can be your files or your machine.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Cybercrimes and Data Breaches”. The manual lists hacking, spreading viruses, computer vandalism, IP theft, and copyright infringement.

cards.question: Say the official sentence about “crimes against property” from memory.
cards.answer: Crimes against property: Property in this case may include information stored within a computer, or the computer itself.
cards.explanation: Property means two things: the information inside a computer, and the computer itself.

cards.question: Official definition: “crimes against government”
cards.answer: Any cybercrime committed against a government organization is considered an attack on that nation's sovereignty.
cards.explanation: Sovereignty is a country's right to rule itself. Attacking its government is an attack on that right.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Cybercrimes and Data Breaches”. The manual lists hacking, theft of confidential information, and cyber terrorism.

cards.question: Say the official sentence about “crimes against government” from memory.
cards.answer: Any cybercrime committed against a government organization is considered an attack on that nation's sovereignty.
cards.explanation: Three ideas: against a government organization, an attack, on the nation's sovereignty.

cards.question: Official definition: “hacktivism”
cards.answer: Hacktivism is another cybercrime that involves hackers seeking to make a political statement with their attacks.
cards.explanation: Hacker plus activism. The attack is a way to defend a cause, not to make money.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Cybercrimes and Data Breaches”. Hacktivists often target government entities, but they may also target other groups they disagree with.

cards.question: Say the official sentence about “hacktivism” from memory.
cards.answer: Hacktivism is another cybercrime that involves hackers seeking to make a political statement with their attacks.
cards.explanation: Three ideas: another cybercrime, hackers, a political statement.

cards.question: Strangers get into a hospital's database and copy the patients' records. Which cybercrime is this?
options: Hacktivism
Online harassment
Credit card fraud
A data breach
options_why: There is no political message. The strangers want the information.
Nobody is insulted or threatened. Records are being taken.
No card is used to pay. The records are copied.
cards.answer: A data breach
cards.explanation: Information is accessed or stolen without permission. This is a data breach.

cards.question: A group attacks a ministry's website to protest a government decision. Which word fits BEST?
options: A data breach
Identity theft
Hacktivism
Cyberstalking
options_why: The goal is to send a message. In a breach, the goal is to take information.
Nobody pretends to be another person here.
No person is followed or watched. A website is attacked.
cards.answer: Hacktivism
cards.explanation: The group wants to make a political statement. That is hacktivism.

cards.question: In a cybercrime, what role can a computer play?
options: It is always the target of the crime, never the tool
It can be the tool or the target of the crime
It is always the tool of the crime
It is never a part of the crime
options_why: A computer can also be the tool, for example to send scam emails.
A computer can also be the target, for example when its data is stolen.
In a cybercrime the computer is at the heart of the crime.
cards.answer: It can be the tool or the target of the crime
cards.explanation: Think of a crowbar. A thief can use it to open a door, or steal it.

cards.question: Which of these is an example of identity theft?
options: Posting insults about a classmate on a chat group
Watching a classmate's every move online
Opening a loan with another person's name
Paying late with your own card
options_why: That is online harassment. No identity is taken.
That is cyberstalking. No identity is taken.
That is not a crime against another person.
cards.answer: Opening a loan with another person's name
cards.explanation: Identity theft means pretending to be another person.

cards.question: Which of these is NOT a crime against people?
options: Cyberstalking
Identity theft
Credit card fraud
Spreading computer viruses
options_why: This is a crime against people. A person is followed online.
This is a crime against people. A person's identity is taken.
This is a crime against people. A person's card is used.
cards.answer: Spreading computer viruses
cards.explanation: Spreading viruses is a crime against property. A virus is a harmful program that copies itself.

cards.question: Which item belongs to crimes against government?
options: Cyber terrorism
Credit card fraud
Online harassment
Copyright infringement
options_why: This is a crime against people.
This is a crime against people.
This is a crime against property.
cards.answer: Cyber terrorism
cards.explanation: Cyber terrorism is on the list of crimes against government.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Cybercrimes and Data Breaches”. The manual does not define cyber terrorism.

cards.question: Which example BEST shows a computer used as the tool of a crime?
options: Breaking into a server to take its data
Cutting the power of a data center
Sending scam emails to steal money
Spreading a virus that wipes a laptop
options_why: Here the server is the target of the crime.
Here the data center is the target of the crime.
Here the laptop is the target of the crime.
cards.answer: Sending scam emails to steal money
cards.explanation: The computer is the tool that does the crime. In the other answers it is the target.

cards.question: Which statement about a data breach is MOST accurate?
options: It is any crime that uses a computer
It only harms very large companies and big banks, never a person
It happens only when hardware breaks
A cybercrime where information is taken without permission
options_why: That describes a cybercrime in general. A breach is one special kind.
The manual says a breach can threaten a person, a company, or a nation.
A breach is a crime. A broken machine is an accident.
cards.answer: A cybercrime where information is taken without permission
cards.explanation: A data breach is one special kind of cybercrime. Its target is the information.

cards.question: The manual puts cybercrimes into three groups. Which is NOT one of them?
options: Crimes against people
Crimes against companies
Crimes against property
Crimes against government
options_why: This is one of the three groups.
This is one of the three groups.
This is one of the three groups.
cards.answer: Crimes against companies
cards.explanation: The three groups are people, property, and government.

cards.question: Why is a cybercrime against a government organization taken very seriously?
options: It is seen as an attack on the nation's sovereignty
Government computers are always faster
Government data is always worth much more money than other data
Only governments can be victims of hacktivism
options_why: Speed has nothing to do with the law.
The reason is not the money. It is the attack on the country.
Hacktivists can also target other groups they disagree with.
cards.answer: It is seen as an attack on the nation's sovereignty
cards.explanation: The government speaks for the whole country. An attack on it is an attack on the country's right to rule itself.

cards.question: Which targets do hacktivists MOST often choose?
options: Random people who still use very old computers at home
Only shops that sell expensive things
Government bodies, or groups they disagree with
Only people who owe them money
options_why: Hacktivists choose targets that fit their cause.
Their goal is a political message, not shopping.
Their goal is a political message, not debts.
cards.answer: Government bodies, or groups they disagree with
cards.explanation: The target follows the cause that the hackers defend.

cards.question: What is hacktivism, in your own words?
cards.answer: Hackers attack to share a political message.
cards.explanation: Think: hacker plus activism. The goal is a message.

cards.question: What is the target of a data breach?
cards.answer: The information system and the data stored inside it.
cards.explanation: The criminal wants the information.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Cybercrimes and Data Breaches”.

cards.question: Who can a data breach or a cybercrime threaten?
cards.answer: A person, a company, or a whole nation.
cards.explanation: The manual says the threat can be small or very large.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Cybercrimes and Data Breaches”.

cards.question: Name one crime against people.
cards.answer: Cyberstalking, online harassment, identity theft, or credit card fraud.
cards.explanation: In all of them, the victim is a person.

concepts.name: The CFAA (Computer Fraud and Abuse Act)

paragraphes: The door of an office is closed. You go in anyway, just to look. You take nothing. Is it wrong? Yes. Going in without permission is called trespassing.
In the 1980s, laws talked mostly about things you can touch. They had to cover the data inside computers too.
In 1986, the United States passed a law for this. It is the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act, or CFAA.

decouverte.comme: A field has a fence around it. Going in without permission is trespassing, even if you break nothing.
decouverte.enVrai: The CFAA punishes getting into a protected computer without permission. It also punishes going beyond the access you were given. Permission is like the fence. You can do wrong without forcing any door, by going further than your rights.

decouverte.question: For the CFAA, which computer is a protected computer?
options: Only a computer of the army
A computer used by the government or a bank, or for trade between states or countries
Only a computer with a password
decouverte.answer: A computer used by the government or a bank, or for trade between states or countries
decouverte.explanation: Protected means that the law protects it. It does not mean that it has a password. The definition is wide, so an ordinary computer can be included.

decouverte.texte: In American law, a crime can be a misdemeanor or a felony. A misdemeanor is less serious. A felony is punished more heavily. The CFAA lists seven offenses. Some start as misdemeanors, but become felonies if the gain is large or if there is fraud. Fraud means lying to get money.

decouverte.comme: Finding another student's locker key is not the same as selling it to someone.
decouverte.enVrai: The CFAA punishes trafficking in passwords. This means passing a password to someone else, or taking control of it to pass it on. Keeping a password with no plan to pass it on is not trafficking.

decouverte.texte: Extortion means getting money by making threats. A criminal says: pay me, or I will damage your computer or share your secrets. The CFAA punishes this.

cards.question: Official definition: “protected computer”
cards.answer: In plain English, a protected computer is a computer used by the U.S. government or financial institutions, or one used for interstate and foreign communications and financial transactions.
cards.explanation: Protected means protected by the law. Think of the government, banks, and trade between states and countries.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “U.S. Computer Fraud and Abuse Act of 1986”. Interstate means between states of the United States.

cards.question: Which sentence is the official definition of “protected computer”?
options: In plain English, a protected computer is a computer used by the U.S. government or financial institutions, or one owned by a private company.
In plain English, a protected computer is a computer with a password, used for interstate and foreign communications and financial transactions.
In plain English, a protected computer is a computer used only by the U.S. military or banks, for foreign communications and financial transactions.
In plain English, a protected computer is a computer used by the U.S. government or financial institutions, or one used for interstate and foreign communications and financial transactions.
options_why: The real sentence is about foreign and interstate use. Owning a computer in a company is not enough.
A password has nothing to do with the definition. The real sentence talks about who uses the computer.
It adds the word only and the military. The real sentence is wider, and also names the government.
cards.answer: In plain English, a protected computer is a computer used by the U.S. government or financial institutions, or one used for interstate and foreign communications and financial transactions.
cards.explanation: Two families: government and finance on one side, interstate and foreign communications on the other.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “protected computer” from memory.
cards.answer: In plain English, a protected computer is a computer used by the U.S. government or financial institutions, or one used for interstate and foreign communications and financial transactions.
cards.explanation: Two families: government and finance on one side, interstate and foreign communications on the other.

cards.question: Official definition: “traffic” (in the CFAA)
cards.answer: The term traffic here means to illegally transfer or obtain control of a password with the intent to transfer it to another party.
cards.explanation: Trafficking means passing a password to someone else. Keeping it for yourself is not trafficking.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “U.S. Computer Fraud and Abuse Act of 1986”. The manual says that owning a password with no plan to pass it on is not included.

cards.question: Which sentence is the official definition of “traffic” (in the CFAA)?
options: The term traffic here means to legally transfer or obtain control of a password with the intent to transfer it to another party.
The term traffic here means to illegally transfer or obtain control of a password with the intent to transfer it to another party.
The term traffic here means to illegally transfer or obtain control of a password without the intent to transfer it to another party.
The term traffic here means to illegally guess or obtain control of a password with the intent to damage another party.
options_why: One word is changed. The real sentence says illegally.
The intent to pass it on is the key idea. The real sentence says with the intent.
Guessing and damage are different ideas. The real sentence is about passing the password on.
cards.answer: The term traffic here means to illegally transfer or obtain control of a password with the intent to transfer it to another party.
cards.explanation: Three ideas: transfer illegally, obtain control, with the intent to pass it on.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “traffic” (in the CFAA) from memory.
cards.answer: The term traffic here means to illegally transfer or obtain control of a password with the intent to transfer it to another party.
cards.explanation: Three ideas: transfer illegally, obtain control, with the intent to pass it on.

cards.question: Official definition: the purpose of the “CFAA”
cards.answer: The CFAA was created to clarify definitions of computer fraud and abuse and to extend existing law to include intangible property such as computer data.
cards.explanation: Two goals: make the words clear, and also protect what you cannot touch, like data.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “U.S. Computer Fraud and Abuse Act of 1986”. Intangible property is property that you cannot touch.

cards.question: Say the official sentence about the purpose of the “CFAA” from memory.
cards.answer: The CFAA was created to clarify definitions of computer fraud and abuse and to extend existing law to include intangible property such as computer data.
cards.explanation: Two goals: clarify the definitions, and extend the law to computer data.

cards.question: A worker may read the payroll files. She also opens the management files, which are off limits to her. Which statement is BEST?
options: She can be punished, because the law covers access beyond your permission
She cannot be punished, because she already had access to that computer and to its files
She cannot be punished, because she sold nothing
She cannot be punished, because she changed no file
options_why: Having access to a computer does not give you the right to open every file.
Selling is not needed. Getting information without permission is enough.
Reading is enough. Nothing has to be changed or damaged.
cards.answer: She can be punished, because the law covers access beyond your permission
cards.explanation: Going beyond the access you were given counts as access without permission.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “U.S. Computer Fraud and Abuse Act of 1986”: access without or in excess of authorization.

cards.question: Before 1996, the CFAA used the term “federal interest computers”. Which term did it use after the 1996 change?
options: Critical computers
Government computers
Protected computers
Network computers
options_why: This is not a term used in the law.
This is too narrow. Banks and trade between states are covered too.
This is not a term used in the law.
cards.answer: Protected computers
cards.explanation: A 1996 change replaced “federal interest computers” with “protected computers”.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “U.S. Computer Fraud and Abuse Act of 1986”.

cards.question: In the CFAA, what does it mean to traffic in passwords?
options: To keep a password that you found, with no plan to pass it on to another person
To guess a password by trying many times
To change your own password too often
To pass a password to someone else, or take control of it to pass it on
options_why: Owning a password with no plan to pass it on is not trafficking.
Guessing is a different act. Trafficking is about passing the password on.
Changing your own password is not a crime.
cards.answer: To pass a password to someone else, or take control of it to pass it on
cards.explanation: Think of the locker key: trafficking means giving or selling it, not only keeping it.

cards.question: What did the CFAA add to the laws of its time?
options: It limited the law to things you can touch
It extended the law to intangible property, like computer data
It made laws only for banks
It stopped companies from watching their own computers and networks
options_why: It did the opposite. Data cannot be touched, and the CFAA covers it.
The CFAA also covers the government and trade between states.
The CFAA does not do this.
cards.answer: It extended the law to intangible property, like computer data
cards.explanation: Before the CFAA, laws talked mostly about things you can touch. Data needed protection too.

cards.question: A criminal lies to a bank to get into a protected computer and takes money. Which CFAA offense is the BEST match?
options: Accessing a computer to commit fraud, (a)(4)
Trespassing in a government computer, (a)(3)
Trafficking in passwords, (a)(6)
Threatening to damage a computer, (a)(7)
options_why: It is about government computers. Here the money is the goal.
Nobody passes a password to another person here.
Nobody makes a threat here. The criminal uses a lie.
cards.answer: Accessing a computer to commit fraud, (a)(4)
cards.explanation: Fraud means lying to get money or something of value. Offense (a)(4) covers this.

cards.question: Which of these is NOT one of the seven CFAA offenses?
options: Threatening to damage a computer to get money
Trafficking in passwords
Selling a used computer to a friend
Obtaining national security information
options_why: This is one of the seven offenses, (a)(7).
This is one of the seven offenses, (a)(6).
This is one of the seven offenses, (a)(1).
cards.answer: Selling a used computer to a friend
cards.explanation: Selling your own used computer is not a crime. The other three are CFAA offenses.

cards.question: Which CFAA offense is the computer version of extortion?
options: Trafficking in passwords, (a)(6)
Accessing a computer to obtain private information, (a)(2)
Trespassing in a government computer, (a)(3)
Threatening to damage a computer to get money, (a)(7)
options_why: This is about passing passwords on. It has no threat.
This is about taking information. It has no threat.
This is about going in without permission. It has no threat.
cards.answer: Threatening to damage a computer to get money, (a)(7)
cards.explanation: Extortion means getting money by making threats. (a)(7) covers threats against a computer or its secrets.

cards.question: Which offense starts as a misdemeanor, and NOT as a felony?
options: Obtaining national security information, (a)(1)
Trafficking in passwords, (a)(6)
Accessing a computer to commit fraud, (a)(4)
Threatening to damage a computer to get money, (a)(7)
options_why: This one is a felony from the start.
This one is a felony from the start.
This one is a felony from the start.
cards.answer: Trafficking in passwords, (a)(6)
cards.explanation: A misdemeanor is less serious than a felony. Password trafficking is a misdemeanor.

cards.question: In offense (a)(2), when does the crime become a felony?
options: When the information is worth more than 5,000 dollars
When the information is worth more than 500 dollars
When more than 10 people see the information
When the information is kept for more than one year
options_why: The number in the manual is 5,000 dollars.
The number of people who see it is not a condition.
Keeping it for a long time is not a condition.
cards.answer: When the information is worth more than 5,000 dollars
cards.explanation: A big value upgrades the crime. A financial gain or another crime also does.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “U.S. Computer Fraud and Abuse Act of 1986”, 1030(a)(2).

cards.question: Offense (a)(5) can become a felony. Which case is one of them?
options: The damage costs less than 5,000 dollars during one whole year
The damage hits 10 or more protected computers in one year
The attacker is a former employee
The attack comes from another country
options_why: A felony needs losses of 5,000 dollars or more.
Who the attacker is does not change the level.
The place of the attacker is not a condition.
cards.answer: The damage hits 10 or more protected computers in one year
cards.explanation: Heavy damage means a heavy punishment. Hurting people or hitting 10 computers counts as heavy.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “U.S. Computer Fraud and Abuse Act of 1986”, 1030(a)(5).

cards.question: Which statement about trespassing in a government computer, (a)(3), is MOST accurate?
options: It needs the attacker to steal information
It only covers computers of banks
It can be charged even if no information is taken
It only covers computers with a password
options_why: Simply going in is enough. Nothing has to be stolen.
It covers computers used by the U.S. government.
The computer must be nonpublic. A password is not the test.
cards.answer: It can be charged even if no information is taken
cards.explanation: It is trespassing in the computer world. The act of going in is the crime.

cards.question: In which year was the CFAA passed?
cards.answer: In 1986, as a change to a law from 1984.
cards.explanation: The 1984 law is the Comprehensive Crime Control Act.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “U.S. Computer Fraud and Abuse Act of 1986”.

cards.question: In which years did the major changes to the CFAA come?
cards.explanation: The minor changes came earlier, in 1988, 1989, and 1999.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “U.S. Computer Fraud and Abuse Act of 1986”.

cards.question: What does offense (a)(1) of the CFAA punish?
cards.answer: Getting national security information without permission, then keeping it or passing it to an unauthorized person.
cards.explanation: It is the most sensitive offense, because it is about state secrets.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “U.S. Computer Fraud and Abuse Act of 1986”, 1030(a)(1).

cards.question: What is a felony, in simple words?
cards.answer: A serious crime that is punished more heavily than a misdemeanor.
cards.explanation: A misdemeanor is the less serious kind.
cards.explanation_more: Outside the manual: this is a simple explanation.

cards.question: Why does the CFAA not punish simply owning a password?
cards.answer: Because trafficking needs the plan to pass the password to someone else.
cards.explanation: Keeping a password for yourself is not the same as selling it.

concepts.name: Other American laws (ECPA, EEA, Patriot Act...)

paragraphes: Long ago, the police could sometimes listen to phone calls in secret. This is called a wiretap. The law set limits on it.
Then people began to send messages over computer networks. Should those messages be protected too?
In 1986, a law said yes. It is the Electronic Communications Privacy Act, or ECPA. The United States then passed many other laws. You will meet them here.

decouverte.comme: In a big building, each corridor has its own sign: “no listening in”, “no copying secrets”, “no unwanted mail”. Each sign protects one precise thing.
decouverte.enVrai: Each law on this planet protects one precise thing: messages, company secrets, identity, or the mailbox. Several laws can also add up on top of each other.

decouverte.question: Which law forbids spying on messages sent over a network?
options: The CFAA, which punishes going in without permission
The ECPA, which forbids intercepting communications
The CAN-SPAM Act, which controls advertising emails
decouverte.answer: The ECPA, which forbids intercepting communications
decouverte.explanation: The CFAA is about going into a computer. The ECPA is about listening to what travels. CAN-SPAM is about unwanted emails, called spam.

cards.question: Official definition: “ECPA”

cards.answer: Under the act, identity theft is "knowingly transfer[ring] or us[ing], without lawful authority, a means of identification of another person with the intent to commit, or to aid or abet, any unlawful activity that constitutes a violation of Federal law, or that constitutes a felony under any applicable State or local law."

cards.question: Official definition: “pen register” (Patriot Act, section 214)

decouverte.titre: The shared rulebook of the tournament

decouverte.enVrai: The Budapest Convention is a treaty, an official agreement between countries. It helps them work together and have more similar laws against cybercrime. Each country still keeps its own laws.

decouverte.question: Which text is the first international treaty against cybercrime?

The British Computer Misuse Act
The Australian Cybercrime Act

decouverte.texte: A country first signs a treaty. Later, it can ratify it. This means it approves the treaty officially. The Budapest Convention was signed in 2001 and took effect in 2004. The United States ratified it in 2006.

The Computer Misuse Act is a law of the United Kingdom, in force since 1990. It lists five offenses. The simplest one is going into a computer without permission, even if nothing is damaged. The others go up to serious damage, and to making tools to attack.

India passed its Information Technology Act in 2000. It gives legal value to electronic documents and digital signatures. A digital signature is an electronic proof that a document comes from its author. Australia passed the Cybercrime Act in 2001, after the attacks of September 11, 2001.

paragraphes: You write a song. A friend copies it and publishes it as if it were theirs. You feel betrayed. It is your work.
On the internet, copying is very easy. Films, games, and software can be copied in a few seconds.
These creations belong to you, even if you cannot touch them. Together, they are called intellectual property, or IP.

decouverte.comme: You lend your bike to a friend, on one condition: they give it back and do not sell it. This permission with conditions is like a license.
decouverte.enVrai: A license is a permission to use something that belongs to someone else, following rules. For software, you pay or accept the conditions, and then you can use it. Software can be copied without the owner losing it, so cheating is tempting.

decouverte.question: The manual quotes an estimate. What share of the software used in the world is not properly licensed?

About 15 percent
More than 40 percent

decouverte.texte: Counterfeit goods are fake copies of real products. Pirated goods are copies made and shared without permission. The manual says counterfeiting is a 460 billion dollar business each year. By 2022, the trade in fake and pirated goods may reach 1.9 to 2.8 trillion dollars.

Unlicensed software does not get updates from its maker. These updates are called patches. They close weak points. In China, about 70 percent of users had unlicensed software, says an estimate. More than 40,000 institutions were hit by the WannaCry malware. Malware means harmful software.

decouverte.titre: The world guardians and the five categories
decouverte.texte: Three world organizations protect intellectual property rights. They are the WTO (World Trade Organization), the WCO (World Customs Organization), and the WIPO (World Intellectual Property Organization). In the United States, the laws fall into five categories: licensing, patents, trademarks, copyrights, and trade secrets.

cards.question: Official definition: “IP”

cards.explanation: Software is a creation of the mind. The law protects it, even if you cannot touch it.

cards.question: Which of these is NOT one of the five categories of American intellectual property law?
options: Patents
Copyrights
Trade secrets
Domain names
options_why: This is one of the five categories. It protects inventions.
This is one of the five categories. It protects original works.
This is one of the five categories. It protects secret recipes and methods.
cards.answer: Domain names
cards.explanation: The five categories are licensing, patents, trademarks, copyrights, and trade secrets.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Licensing and Intellectual Property Requirements”.

cards.question: What is a license?
options: The ownership of something that belongs to someone else, once you have paid for it
A fine paid after copying a program
A permission to use something that belongs to someone else, with rules
A free copy that anyone can share
options_why: A license does not make you the owner.
A fine is a punishment. A license is a permission.
A license sets rules. It does not allow free sharing.
cards.answer: A permission to use something that belongs to someone else, with rules
cards.explanation: Think of lending a bike with conditions. Without the license, using the product is illegal.
cards.explanation_more: Outside the manual: this is a simple explanation. The manual presents licensing as the first of the five categories.

cards.question: What does the word counterfeit mean?
options: A fake copy of a product, sold as the real one
A product sold at a very low price
A product sent across a border
A real product sold without a shop
options_why: A low price is not the point. A counterfeit pretends to be real.
Crossing a border is a different idea.
A counterfeit is fake, not real.
cards.answer: A fake copy of a product, sold as the real one
cards.explanation: Counterfeiting is a business of 460 billion dollars a year, says the manual.

cards.question: A small company installs a copied program to save money. A year later, a weak point is found in the program. What BEST describes the result?
options: The maker sends the fix to it for free
It gets no fix, so the weak point stays open
Its antivirus repairs the program by itself
The weak point closes after one year
options_why: Makers send fixes to customers with a legal license.
An antivirus does not remove the weak points of a program.
Weak points do not close by themselves.
cards.answer: It gets no fix, so the weak point stays open
cards.explanation: Legal versions get patches. Illegal copies do not get the updates.

cards.question: Which problem is MOST likely for a company that uses unlicensed software?
options: Its programs will stop working at once
It will need more computers
It will lose its own copyrights
It will not get security patches and updates
options_why: The programs still work. The problem is the missing updates.
Unlicensed software does not need more machines.
Its own rights stay the same.
cards.answer: It will not get security patches and updates
cards.explanation: Without patches, weak points stay open and attackers can use them.

cards.question: According to the manual, what is one of the biggest problems for licensing?
options: Not enough technology to make licenses
Too few companies that make software
A lack of enforcement of the rules
Software that is too cheap to sell
options_why: The manual says new tools exist. The problem is enforcement.
The number of makers is not the problem.
Price is not mentioned as the biggest problem.
cards.answer: A lack of enforcement of the rules
cards.explanation: Tools exist to manage licenses. The rules are not enforced enough.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Licensing”.

cards.question: The Business Software Alliance says that a share of the software used in the world is not properly licensed. How big is it?
options: More than 40 percent
About 5 percent
About 15 percent
Almost 90 percent
options_why: This is much too low. More than 4 programs out of 10 are not licensed.
This is too low. The estimate is more than 40 percent.
This is too high. The estimate is more than 40 percent.
cards.answer: More than 40 percent
cards.explanation: More than 4 programs out of 10 are used without a proper license.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Licensing”. The Business Software Alliance is also called the BSA.

cards.question: Which organization is NOT named in the manual as protecting intellectual property rights around the world?
options: The World Trade Organization
The World Health Organization
The World Customs Organization
The World Intellectual Property Organization
options_why: It is named in the manual. Its short name is WTO.
It is named in the manual. Its short name is WCO.
It is named in the manual. Its short name is WIPO.
cards.answer: The World Health Organization
cards.explanation: The three organizations in the manual are the WTO, the WCO, and the WIPO.

cards.question: Why was unlicensed software a problem in the WannaCry attacks in China?
options: The software was too old to run
The makers shared the users' passwords
Its users could not get the patches that close weak points
A license gives an attacker access to the software and all its updates
options_why: The software ran. It had open weak points.
Makers do not share passwords.
A license does not give anyone access.
cards.answer: Its users could not get the patches that close weak points
cards.explanation: No license means no updates. The malware found open weak points. Malware is harmful software.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Licensing”. About 70 percent of users in China ran unlicensed software, says an estimate.

cards.question: Which choice is LEAST likely to protect a company from weak points in software?
options: Installing the patches sent by the maker
Buying licensed software
Updating programs often
Using copies of software without a license
options_why: Patches close weak points. This helps a lot.
A licensed copy gets updates from the maker.
Updates close weak points. This helps a lot.
cards.answer: Using copies of software without a license
cards.explanation: A copy without a license gets no updates. Its weak points stay open.

cards.question: What does the manual say counterfeiting is worth each year?
options: 460 billion dollars
46 billion dollars
4.6 billion dollars
4.6 trillion dollars
options_why: This is ten times too low.
This is a hundred times too low.
This is ten times too high.
cards.answer: 460 billion dollars
cards.explanation: Online shops and fast international shipping made counterfeiting easier.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Licensing”.

cards.question: What is intellectual property, in your own words?
cards.answer: Creations of the mind that belong to someone, like software, music, films, or drawings.
cards.explanation: You cannot touch them, but they have value and the law protects them.

cards.question: What does WIPO stand for?
cards.answer: World Intellectual Property Organization.
cards.explanation: The key words are Intellectual Property.
cards.explanation_more: The manual also names the WTO (World Trade Organization) and the WCO (World Customs Organization).

cards.question: By 2022, how big could the trade in fake and pirated goods be?
cards.answer: Between 1.9 and 2.8 trillion dollars.
cards.explanation: A pirated product is a copy made illegally, such as a film or a game.
cards.explanation_more: A trillion is a thousand billion. Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Licensing”.

cards.question: What share of all bandwidth is used by activities that break IP rights?
cards.answer: About 23 percent, says an estimate in the manual.
cards.explanation: Bandwidth is the amount of data that travels on the internet. Nearly a quarter of it is used for this.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Licensing”.

cards.question: Why does unlicensed software increase the risk of an attack?
cards.answer: Its users do not get the maker's patches and updates. The weak points stay open.
cards.explanation: Legal versions get fixed. Illegal copies do not.
cards.explanation_more: The manual finds it ironic: by using software illegally, people become an easier target for other criminals.

concepts.name: The patent and the trade secret

paragraphes: You invent a ball that always bounces straight. You are proud. But what if your neighbor makes copies to sell? How can you protect your invention?
There are two paths. You can ask the government for an exclusive right for a limited time. This is a patent. Or you can keep the method secret. This is a trade secret.

decouverte.comme: Your ball is an invention. The government gives you the exclusive right to make it for some years. A pizza place has a secret recipe. Nobody knows it, and it is worth a lot while it stays hidden.
decouverte.enVrai: A patent is a right given by the government, for a fixed time. A trade secret is information that the company keeps for itself. A secret recipe does not end after twenty years, but a patent does.

decouverte.question: How long does a patent usually last in the United States?
options: Forever
15 or 20 years
One year, and it can be renewed
decouverte.explanation: A patent lasts for a fixed time. The first answer is tempting, because you may think of a protection with no end.

decouverte.titre: The three conditions for a patent
decouverte.texte: To get a patent, an invention must be new: nobody has made it before. It must be useful: it serves a purpose. It must be nonobvious: not an idea that anyone would have had right away.

decouverte.titre: A pass that works in one country only
decouverte.comme: The bus pass of your town does not work in the next town. You need to buy another one.
decouverte.enVrai: A U.S. patent only works in the United States and its territories. To be protected elsewhere, you must apply in each country, for example at the European Patent Office, or EPO.

decouverte.texte: The Coca-Cola recipe has been kept secret since 1886. It is valuable to the company only because nobody else knows it. The manual gives it as an example of a trade secret.

cards.question: Official definition: “patent”
cards.answer: A patent is a government-issued license or grant of property rights to an inventor that prohibits another party from making, using, importing, or selling the invention for a set period of time.
cards.explanation: Only the inventor can make or sell the invention, for a limited time. The government gives this right.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Patents”. In the United States, the USPTO issues patents.

cards.question: Which sentence is the official definition of “patent”?
options: A patent is a government-issued license or grant of property rights to an inventor that prohibits another party from making, using, importing, or selling the invention forever.
A patent is a government-issued license or grant of property rights to an inventor that prohibits another party from making, using, importing, or selling the invention for a set period of time.
A patent is a government-issued license or grant of property rights to an inventor that allows another party to make, use, import, or sell the invention for a set period of time.
A patent is a company-issued license or grant of property rights to an inventor that prohibits another party from making, using, importing, or selling the invention for a set period of time.
options_why: It says forever. The real sentence says for a set period of time.
It says allows. A patent prohibits other people from doing these acts.
It says company-issued. A patent comes from the government.
cards.answer: A patent is a government-issued license or grant of property rights to an inventor that prohibits another party from making, using, importing, or selling the invention for a set period of time.
cards.explanation: Four verbs to remember: making, using, importing, selling.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “patent” from memory.
cards.answer: A patent is a government-issued license or grant of property rights to an inventor that prohibits another party from making, using, importing, or selling the invention for a set period of time.
cards.explanation: Four verbs to remember: making, using, importing, selling.

cards.question: Official definition: “trade secret”
cards.answer: A trade secret is a proprietary formula, process, practice, or combination of information that a company has exclusive rights to.
cards.explanation: It is a recipe or a method that belongs to one company. Only that company has the rights to it.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Trade secrets”. Proprietary means that it belongs to the company.

cards.question: Which sentence is the official definition of “trade secret”?
options: A trade secret is a proprietary formula, process, practice, or combination of information that a company has exclusive rights to for 20 years.
A trade secret is a public formula, process, practice, or combination of information that a company has exclusive rights to.
A trade secret is a proprietary formula, process, practice, or combination of information that the government has exclusive rights to.
A trade secret is a proprietary formula, process, practice, or combination of information that a company has exclusive rights to.
options_why: A trade secret has no end date. The 20 years idea comes from patents.
A trade secret is not public. It stays hidden.
The company has the rights, not the government.
cards.answer: A trade secret is a proprietary formula, process, practice, or combination of information that a company has exclusive rights to.
cards.explanation: Four kinds of secrets: formula, process, practice, combination of information.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “trade secret” from memory.
cards.answer: A trade secret is a proprietary formula, process, practice, or combination of information that a company has exclusive rights to.
cards.explanation: Four kinds of secrets: formula, process, practice, combination of information.

cards.question: A company invents a new battery. It wants a right to make it that no one else has, given by the government for a limited time. What does it choose?
options: A trade secret
A trademark
A patent
A license
options_why: Nobody grants a secret. The company simply keeps it hidden.
A trademark shows who sells a product. It does not protect the invention.
A license is a permission to use something that belongs to someone else.
cards.answer: A patent
cards.explanation: An exclusive right, given by the government for a fixed time, is exactly a patent.

cards.question: A pizza place keeps its recipe hidden from everyone outside the team. Which protection is this?
options: A trade secret
A patent
A trademark
A copyright
options_why: A patent is a right given by the government. The pizza place asked for nothing.
A trademark protects a sign, not a recipe.
A copyright protects an original work, such as a book or a song.
cards.answer: A trade secret
cards.explanation: A trade secret stays hidden. It is worth money only while nobody else knows it.

cards.question: Which of these is NOT a condition to get a patent?
options: The invention must be new
The invention must be useful
The invention must be famous
The invention must be nonobvious
options_why: This is a condition. Nobody has made it before.
This is a condition. It must serve a purpose.
This is a condition. It is not an idea that anyone would have right away.
cards.answer: The invention must be famous
cards.explanation: A patent needs three things: new, useful, and nonobvious. Fame is not a condition.

cards.question: What does nonobvious mean for a patent?
options: Hidden from the public until the patent is issued
Not yet sold in any shop in the whole country
Too hard for most people to use or understand
Not an idea that anyone would have at once
options_why: That is the idea of a trade secret, not of a patent.
That is the idea of new, not of nonobvious.
A patent needs a useful invention.
cards.answer: Not an idea that anyone would have at once
cards.explanation: If every person could think of it at once, it is not worth a patent.

cards.question: How long does a U.S. patent usually last?
options: 1 year, and it can be renewed
15 or 20 years
50 years
As long as the inventor lives
options_why: A patent lasts much longer than one year.
This is too long. The manual says 15 or 20 years.
That is not how a patent works. It has a set end.
cards.answer: 15 or 20 years
cards.explanation: A patent lasts for a fixed time, and then it ends.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Patents”.

cards.question: An inventor has a U.S. patent. She wants to sell her invention in France. What should she BEST do?
options: Apply for a patent in France too
Do nothing, because a U.S. patent is valid worldwide
Ask the USPTO to extend it to every country
Sell in France and go to court later
options_why: A U.S. patent is only valid in the United States and its territories.
The USPTO cannot do this. She must apply in each country.
Without a patent in France, she has no protection there.
cards.answer: Apply for a patent in France too
cards.explanation: She must apply in each country where she wants to be protected.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Patents”.

cards.question: Who enforces patent law in the United States?
options: The USPTO
The U.S. legal system
The Federal Trade Commission
The company that owns the patent, alone
options_why: The USPTO issues patents. It does not enforce them.
It enforces the CAN-SPAM Act, not patents.
The owner can sue, but the courts enforce the law.
cards.answer: The U.S. legal system
cards.explanation: The USPTO issues patents. The courts defend them.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Patents”.

cards.question: Which tool MOST suits information that is valuable only while it stays hidden?
options: A patent
A license
A trademark
A trade secret
options_why: A patent needs a public description of the invention.
A license is a permission to use. It does not hide anything.
A trademark shows who sells a product. It is public.
cards.answer: A trade secret
cards.explanation: A trade secret is worth money only because it stays hidden.
cards.explanation_more: Outside the manual: a patent application describes the invention in public, so it cannot stay secret.

cards.question: A foreign company sells a product that breaks a U.S. patent. Which body can order the product to be kept out of the United States?
options: The USPTO
The Federal Trade Commission
The U.S. International Trade Commission
The World Intellectual Property Organization
options_why: It issues patents. It does not stop products at the border.
It enforces the CAN-SPAM Act.
It is a world body. It does not give orders for the United States.
cards.answer: The U.S. International Trade Commission
cards.explanation: The ITC can issue orders that keep the product out of the country.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Patents”. The strongest remedy may still come from the courts.

cards.question: The Coca-Cola recipe has been kept since 1886. Why is it a trade secret?
options: It is proprietary and has value only because it is secret
The government gave it to the company for a period of 20 years
It is a sign that shows who sells the drink
It was copied from a foreign company
options_why: That describes a patent.
That describes a trademark.
The manual says nothing like this.
cards.answer: It is proprietary and has value only because it is secret
cards.explanation: The company owns it, and it is worth money only while it stays secret.

cards.question: Who mostly handles trade secret laws in the United States?
options: The USPTO
The states
The International Trade Commission
The World Intellectual Property Organization
options_why: It handles patents and trademarks.
It acts on products at the border.
It is a world body, not a U.S. one.
cards.answer: The states
cards.explanation: Most states use the Uniform Trade Secrets Act, or UTSA. Two federal laws also make theft a federal crime.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Trade secrets”.

cards.question: A company wants to protect a recipe for more than 100 years. Which choice is BEST?
options: Get a patent, because it never ends
Get a patent, because it lasts 100 years
Ask the USPTO to keep it for free
Keep it as a trade secret
options_why: A patent ends after 15 or 20 years.
A patent does not last 100 years.
The USPTO issues patents. It does not keep secrets.
cards.answer: Keep it as a trade secret
cards.explanation: A secret can last as long as nobody finds it out. A patent ends after a set time.

cards.question: What are the three conditions to get a patent?
cards.answer: The invention must be new, useful, and nonobvious.
cards.explanation: Nonobvious means that not just anyone would have thought of it right away.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Patents”.

cards.question: Name one patent office outside the United States.
cards.answer: The European Patent Office (EPO), the Eurasian Patent Organization (EAPO), or ARIPO.
cards.explanation: Each big region has its own office.
cards.explanation_more: ARIPO stands for African Regional Intellectual Property Organization. Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Patents”.

cards.question: What is the main difference between a patent and a trade secret?
cards.answer: A patent is a right from the government, for a limited time. A trade secret is information that the company keeps hidden itself.
cards.explanation: One is public and ends. The other is hidden and can last longer.

cards.question: In which year was the Uniform Trade Secrets Act last amended?
cards.explanation: Most states adopted it as a shared model.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Trade secrets”.

cards.question: Which U.S. federal laws make theft of trade secrets a crime?
cards.answer: The Economic Espionage Act of 1996 and the Defend Trade Secrets Act of 2016.
cards.explanation: Two federal laws: 1996, then 2016.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Trade secrets”.

paragraphes: You see two pairs of almost identical sneakers. One has the logo of your favorite brand. The other has none. The logo tells you who made the pair.
If someone sticks this logo on fake sneakers, you would be fooled. To prevent this, the law protects the signs that show who sells a product.
This protected sign is called a trademark.

decouverte.comme: A signature at the bottom of a drawing shows who made it. Nobody else has the right to sign in your place.
decouverte.enVrai: A trademark is a word, a phrase, a symbol, or a design. It shows who sells a product and sets it apart from the products of others. For a service, we talk about a service mark. The trademark does not protect the object itself. It only shows who sells it.

decouverte.question: Does a trademark end after a fixed time, like a patent?
options: Yes, after 20 years, like a patent
No, it lasts as long as it is used in commerce
decouverte.answer: No, it lasts as long as it is used in commerce
decouverte.explanation: A patent has a fixed length. A trademark can last forever, if it is used. The first answer is tempting, because you may think that every protection ends.

decouverte.texte: The word Coca-Cola is a trademark. It sets this drink apart from Pepsi and all the other colas. A taxi company has a service mark. Its name shows who provides the service. In daily life, people often say trademark for both.

In the United States, the USPTO handles patents and trademarks. USPTO stands for United States Patent and Trademark Office. A patent protects an invention for a fixed time. A trademark protects a sign for as long as it is used.

cards.question: Official definition: “trademark”
cards.answer: According to the USPTO, a trademark is "a word, phrase, symbol, and/or design that identifies and distinguishes the source of the goods of one party from those of others."
cards.explanation: It is the logo or name on your sneakers. It shows who makes them and sets them apart from other brands.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Trademarks”. USPTO stands for United States Patent and Trademark Office.

cards.question: Which sentence is the official definition of “trademark”?
options: According to the USPTO, a trademark is "a word, phrase, symbol, and/or design that identifies and distinguishes the source of the services of one party from those of others."
According to the USPTO, a trademark is "a word, phrase, symbol, and/or design that identifies and distinguishes the inventor of the goods of one party from those of others."
According to the USPTO, a trademark is "a word, phrase, symbol, and/or design that identifies and distinguishes the source of the goods of one party from those of others."
According to the USPTO, a trademark is "a word or phrase, but not a design, that identifies and distinguishes the source of the goods of one party from those of others."
options_why: It says services. The real sentence says goods. Services have another name: service mark.
It says inventor. A trademark shows the source of the goods, not the inventor.
It says not a design. The real sentence names word, phrase, symbol, and/or design.
cards.answer: According to the USPTO, a trademark is "a word, phrase, symbol, and/or design that identifies and distinguishes the source of the goods of one party from those of others."
cards.explanation: Three ideas: word, phrase, symbol, and/or design; identifies and distinguishes; the source of the goods.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “trademark” from memory.
cards.answer: According to the USPTO, a trademark is "a word, phrase, symbol, and/or design that identifies and distinguishes the source of the goods of one party from those of others."
cards.explanation: Three ideas: word, phrase, symbol, and/or design; identifies and distinguishes; the source of the goods.

cards.question: Official definition: “service mark”
cards.answer: A service mark is a similar legal grant that identifies and distinguishes the source of a service rather than goods.
cards.explanation: It is the same idea as a trademark, but for a service, such as a taxi ride or a delivery.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Trademarks”. The manual says the word trademark is commonly used for both.

cards.question: Which sentence is the official definition of “service mark”?
options: A service mark is a similar legal grant that identifies and distinguishes the source of a service rather than goods.
A service mark is a similar legal grant that identifies and distinguishes the source of goods rather than a service.
A service mark is a similar legal grant that identifies and distinguishes the owner of a service rather than goods.
A service mark is a different legal grant that identifies and distinguishes the source of a service and of goods.
options_why: The two words are swapped. A service mark is for a service.
It says owner. The real sentence says source.
It says different and adds goods. The real sentence says similar, and a service rather than goods.
cards.answer: A service mark is a similar legal grant that identifies and distinguishes the source of a service rather than goods.
cards.explanation: Three ideas: a similar legal grant, identifies and distinguishes the source, a service rather than goods.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “service mark” from memory.
cards.answer: A service mark is a similar legal grant that identifies and distinguishes the source of a service rather than goods.
cards.explanation: Three ideas: a similar legal grant, identifies and distinguishes the source, a service rather than goods.

cards.question: What does a trademark show?
options: Who invented a product
Who sells a product
Who wrote the manual of a product
How long a product will last
options_why: That is the job of a patent.
A manual is not the point. A trademark is about the seller.
A trademark says nothing about quality or time.
cards.answer: Who sells a product
cards.explanation: Think of a signature. It says who is behind the product.

cards.question: What protects the well-known logo of a sneaker brand?
options: A patent
A trade secret
A license
A trademark
options_why: A patent protects an invention, not a sign.
A logo is public. A trade secret stays hidden.
A license is a permission to use something.
cards.answer: A trademark
cards.explanation: The logo shows who sells the sneakers. That is the job of a trademark.

cards.question: The name of a taxi company shows who provides a service. Which term is the MOST precise?
options: A trademark for goods
A patent
A service mark
A trade secret
options_why: Goods are things you buy. A taxi ride is a service.
A patent protects an invention.
A company name is public. It is not hidden.
cards.answer: A service mark
cards.explanation: A service mark is for a service. In daily life, people often say trademark for both.

cards.question: A small company puts a logo almost identical to a big brand's logo on its juice bottles. What does trademark protection BEST help to prevent?
options: Customers mixing up who makes the product
Other companies copying the juice recipe
Other companies inventing a new bottle
Other companies selling juice at a lower price
options_why: Protecting a recipe is the job of a trade secret.
Protecting an invention is the job of a patent.
A trademark does not control prices.
cards.answer: Customers mixing up who makes the product
cards.explanation: A trademark shows who sells. A logo that is too close can fool customers.

cards.question: How long do trademark rights last?
options: Exactly 10 years, and then it must be renewed
15 or 20 years
As long as the mark is used in commerce
Until the owner of the sign dies or sells it
options_why: A trademark has no fixed end date.
That is the length of a patent.
The death of the owner is not the test. Use in commerce is.
cards.answer: As long as the mark is used in commerce
cards.explanation: A trademark can last forever, if it is still used.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Trademarks”.

cards.question: Which of these is NOT a kind of sign that a trademark can be?
options: A word
A symbol
A design
A secret formula
options_why: A word can be a trademark.
A symbol can be a trademark.
A design can be a trademark.
cards.answer: A secret formula
cards.explanation: A trademark is a public sign. A secret formula is a trade secret.

cards.question: Which example is MOST likely a trademark?
options: The secret recipe of Coca-Cola
The word Coca-Cola on a bottle
A new machine that fills bottles
The text of a song
options_why: A recipe kept hidden is a trade secret.
A new machine is an invention. A patent can protect it.
A song text is an original work. Copyright protects it.
cards.answer: The word Coca-Cola on a bottle
cards.explanation: The word sets this drink apart from Pepsi and all other colas.

cards.question: A company has a new invention and a new brand name. Which pair of protections is BEST?
options: A patent for the invention and a trademark for the name
A trademark for the invention and a patent for the name
A patent for both the invention and the name
A trademark for both the invention and the name
options_why: The two are swapped. A patent is for an invention.
A patent does not protect a name that shows who sells.
A trademark does not protect an invention.
cards.answer: A patent for the invention and a trademark for the name
cards.explanation: Invention: patent. Sign that shows the seller: trademark.

cards.question: Which office handles both U.S. patents and U.S. trademarks?
options: The Federal Trade Commission
The USPTO
The International Trade Commission
The Copyright Office
options_why: It enforces the CAN-SPAM Act.

cards.question: What is a trademark, in simple words?
cards.answer: A sign, like a word, a logo, or a design, that shows who sells a product.

cards.question: What does USPTO stand for?

cards.question: What is the difference between a service mark and a trademark?
cards.answer: A service mark is for a service, like a taxi. A trademark is for goods. People often say trademark for both.
cards.explanation: Same idea, two kinds of things to identify.

paragraphes: You write the lyrics of a song. You file nothing and sign nothing. A classmate sings them on stage and says he wrote them. Is that allowed?
No. As soon as you create an original work, the law protects you, even without an official paper. This protection is called copyright.

decouverte.comme: The lyrics are your own text. Nobody can copy and sell them without your agreement.
decouverte.enVrai: Copyright protects original works: books, films, songs, poems, artistic creations, and software. So software is protected like a book. The protection is not only for the arts. It also covers the code of an app.

decouverte.question: In the United States, do you need to register a work to be protected by copyright?

No, the protection exists without registration
decouverte.answer: No, the protection exists without registration
decouverte.explanation: You can register a work with the U.S. Copyright Office, but you do not have to. The first answer is tempting, because you may think that a right always needs a paper.

decouverte.texte: A developer writes a game app. Her code is an original work, so copyright protects it. Copying this code and selling it without her agreement can violate her copyright. For a work created by one person, the protection lasts for the whole life of the author, plus 70 years.
A patent lasts 15 or 20 years. A trademark lasts as long as it is used in commerce. A copyright lasts for the life of the author plus 70 years. Each protection has its own length.

cards.question: Official definition: “copyright”
cards.answer: A copyright is a legal protection granted to the authors of "original works of authorship" that may include books, movies, songs, poetry, artistic creations, and computer software, among other categories.
cards.explanation: Think of the lyrics of your song. It is an original work, and it is protected from the moment you create it.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Copyrights”. The manual says a work does not need to be registered to be protected.

cards.explanation: The manual lists computer software among the works that copyright protects.

concepts.name: Import/export and data flows between countries (transborder data flow)

paragraphes: You go on a trip. At customs, an officer looks at what you carry. Some things cannot enter a country, or cannot leave it.
Now imagine that your file holds the plans of a satellite. A simple email can send it to another country in one second.
Many countries watch the movement of technology across their borders. These are called import/export controls.

decouverte.comme: At customs, an officer decides what can come in or go out. Some objects pass, others are refused, depending on the country.
decouverte.enVrai: A country can forbid importing or exporting some technologies, like encryption. Data also crosses borders. This is called transborder data flow. On the internet, the border cannot be seen, and an email can already be an export.

decouverte.question: For the American ITAR rule, what can count as an export?
options: Sending a controlled plan abroad by email
Only shipping a package by boat
Only selling a product in a foreign store
decouverte.answer: Sending a controlled plan abroad by email
decouverte.explanation: For ITAR, even a simple email with controlled data is an export. The other two answers are tempting, because you think of objects that you can see travelling.

decouverte.texte: ITAR means International Traffic in Arms Regulations. It controls the export of defense equipment and services, like satellites, planes, or missiles. An email with a controlled 3D plan is an export. This data must not go to Iran, Syria, North Korea, and other named countries.

decouverte.comme: The school cafeteria requires that meals are prepared in its own kitchen, and not somewhere else.
decouverte.enVrai: Some countries require that some data is processed inside their borders. This is called data localization. More than 34 countries have a rule like this.

decouverte.texte: Cloud providers have data centers all over the world. To follow ITAR, several offer a GovCloud. This is an area of the cloud limited to one region. The data stays in the country.

cards.question: Official definition: “import/export controls”
cards.answer: Many countries closely regulate the movement of technology through their borders.
cards.explanation: Think of customs. A country decides which technologies can cross its borders.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Import/Export Controls”. Reasons: protect local industries, limit sensitive technologies like encryption, or other goals of the country.

cards.explanation: One idea: many countries closely regulate the movement of technology through their borders.

cards.question: Official definition: “ITAR”
cards.answer: ITAR regulates the export of defense articles and defense services to keep those sensitive materials out of the hands of foreign nationals.
cards.explanation: ITAR means International Traffic in Arms Regulations. These rules control the export of defense equipment and services.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Import/Export Controls”. ITAR applies to government agencies, contractors, and their subcontractors.

cards.question: Which sentence is the official definition of “ITAR”?
options: ITAR regulates the export of defense articles and defense services to keep those sensitive materials out of the hands of foreign nationals.
ITAR regulates the import of defense articles and defense services to keep those sensitive materials out of the hands of foreign nationals.
ITAR regulates the export of consumer articles and consumer services to keep those sensitive materials out of the hands of foreign nationals.
ITAR regulates the export of defense articles and defense services to keep those sensitive materials out of the hands of all U.S. citizens.
options_why: It says import. The real sentence says export.
It says consumer. The real sentence says defense.
It says U.S. citizens. The real sentence says foreign nationals.
cards.answer: ITAR regulates the export of defense articles and defense services to keep those sensitive materials out of the hands of foreign nationals.
cards.explanation: Three ideas: the export of defense articles and services, sensitive materials, foreign nationals.

cards.question: Say the official definition of “ITAR” from memory.
cards.answer: ITAR regulates the export of defense articles and defense services to keep those sensitive materials out of the hands of foreign nationals.
cards.explanation: Three ideas: the export of defense articles and services, sensitive materials, foreign nationals.

cards.question: Official definition: “sanctions”
cards.answer: The United States, European Union, and other jurisdictions sometimes issue sanctions (government edicts that prohibit doing business with a given person, group, organization, or country) against particular countries or particular entities.
cards.explanation: A sanction says: it is forbidden to do business with this person, group, or country.
cards.explanation_more: Source: (ISC)2 manual, domain 1, section “Import/Export Controls”. Sanctions change much more often than import/export laws.

cards.question: Say the official sentence about “sanctions” from memory.
cards.answer: The United States, European Union, and other jurisdictions sometimes issue sanctions (government edicts that prohibit doing business with a given person, group, organization, or country) against particular countries or particular entities.
cards.explanation: Three ideas: sanctions, government edicts, a ban on doing business.

cards.question: A government forbids all companies to do business with one named country. Which word BEST describes this?
options: An import/export control
Data localization
A sanction
A license
options_why: It controls the movement of technology, not all business.
It is about where data is kept.
A license is a permission to use something.
cards.answer: A sanction
cards.explanation: A sanction targets a person, group, organization, or country. It forbids doing business with it.

cards.question: An engineer emails the 3D plan of a missile part to a colleague abroad. What does ITAR say?
options: It is not an export, because only packages count
It is allowed if the engineer is not paid for it
It is allowed if the colleague works for the same company
It is an export, and it is under control
options_why: The manual is clear: an email with controlled data is already an export.
Payment changes nothing. The content of the email is controlled.
The company is not the test. The place and the person are.
cards.answer: It is an export, and it is under control
cards.explanation: For ITAR, a simple email with controlled data counts as an export.

cards.question: Some countries require data about their citizens to be stored inside the country. What is this called?
options: A sanction
Data localization
An ITAR order
A patent
options_why: A sanction forbids doing business with a person or a country.
ITAR is about defense articles and services.
A patent protects an invention.
cards.answer: Data localization
cards.explanation: More than 34 countries have some kind of data localization rule.

cards.question: Which of these does ITAR control?
options: The export of defense articles and services
The import of food and drink into a country
The sale of music
The use of strong passwords
options_why: ITAR is about defense, not food.
ITAR is about defense, not music.
ITAR is not about passwords.
cards.answer: The export of defense articles and services
cards.explanation: Satellites, aircraft, spacecraft, and missiles are examples of controlled items.

cards.question: Which statement about ITAR data in the cloud is BEST?
options: It can be stored in any country, if the provider is a large company
It can be stored anywhere, except in three countries
It must stay in the United States, or it counts as an export
It must be deleted after one year

cards.answer: It must stay in the United States, or it counts as an export
